questions.question: Organization of life is the existence of life from a single-celled organism to what type of organism?
options: A non-living colony of identical particles
questions.explanation: Life is organized from the cell to multicellular organisms with complex structures. A multicellular organism is the correct endpoint.

questions.question: How many levels of organization of life in organisms are mentioned?
questions.explanation: The levels mentioned are cell, tissue, organ, and system; that is four levels.

questions.question: The smallest unit of living organisms is defined as the:
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an organism at the cellular level?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a single-celled organism, so it exists at the cellular level.

questions.question: Pandorina and Volvox are examples of single-celled organisms that live:
questions.explanation: Pandorina and Volvox are colonial organisms; many cells live together in a colony.

questions.question: Spirogyra exists as a:
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga, existing as a filament.

questions.question: A group of similar cells that perform a particular function is defined as a:
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing a particular function.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms exists at the tissue level of organization?
questions.explanation: Fungi show tissue-level organization; the others are unicellular.

questions.question: In man, which type of tissue lines and protects the body surface?
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue, or epithelium, lines and protects body surfaces.

questions.question: The main function of blood tissue in man is to:
options: Support the body and aid movement
questions.explanation: Blood is a connective tissue that transports food, oxygen, wastes, and hormones.

questions.question: Which tissue coordinates and transmits nerve impulses in man?
questions.explanation: Nerve tissue coordinates and transmits nerve impulses.

questions.question: In plants, the transport of manufactured food from leaves to other parts is carried out by the:
questions.explanation: Phloem transports manufactured food from leaves to other parts of the plant.

questions.question: The process by which the phloem transports manufactured food in plants is called:
questions.explanation: Translocation is the transport of manufactured food through the phloem.

questions.question: Collenchyma and parenchyma are examples of which type of plant tissue?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma and parenchyma are ground tissues often grouped as strengthening or supporting tissues in this classification.

questions.question: Which plant tissue provides a surface for new cells which are used for storage?
questions.explanation: Packing tissue provides a surface for new cells and is used for storage.

questions.question: A group of similar tissue forming a layer in an organism which performs a specific function is an:
questions.explanation: An organ is a group of similar tissues forming a layer or structure that performs a specific function.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an organ in a plant?
questions.explanation: An onion bulb is an organ. Root system is a system, while xylem and phloem are tissues.

questions.question: The kidney, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra constitute which system of mammals?
questions.explanation: These organs form the excretory system, which removes waste products.

questions.question: The root system and shoot system are examples of systems found in:
questions.explanation: Root and shoot systems are plant organ systems.

questions.question: In higher organisms, a group of similar cells are differentiated to form tissues as a result of:
questions.explanation: As organisms become more complex, cells differentiate to form tissues.

questions.question: Internal structural specialization in complex organisms occurs when a group of similar cells or tissues become specialized to:
options: Shrink in overall size and disappear
questions.explanation: Specialized cells and tissues are adapted to perform specific functions.

questions.question: In complex organisms, mutual interdependence between component cells results in:
questions.explanation: Interdependence among cells leads to a division of labour among tissues and organs.

questions.question: Complexity leads to an increase in size in higher organisms because:
questions.explanation: Spaces between cells allow growth and increase in overall size.

questions.question: In unicellular organisms, reproduction leads to the disintegration of the parent(s) because:
options: Only specialized reproductive parts are involved
They have a very long life span
questions.explanation: In unicellular organisms, the whole parent cell is involved in reproduction, so it divides or disintegrates.

questions.question: Due to the specialization and efficiency of tissues, organs, and systems, complex organisms generally have:
options: A shorter life span than unicellular organisms
The exact same life span as unicellular organisms
questions.explanation: Specialization and efficient systems generally give complex organisms a longer life span.

questions.question: A disadvantage of complexity is that individual cells lose their independence and become:
options: Able to exist on their own easily
questions.explanation: Complexity makes cells more dependent on one another for survival.

questions.question: Compared to unicellular organisms, multicellular organisms have a:
options: Large surface area to volume ratio
Small surface area to volume ratio
Identical surface area to volume ratio
Variable surface area to volume ratio
questions.explanation: Multicellular organisms have a smaller surface area to volume ratio than unicellular organisms.

questions.question: Because complex organisms have a small surface area to volume ratio that makes diffusion inefficient, they have developed:
questions.explanation: Transport systems help move materials efficiently when diffusion alone is insufficient.

questions.question: Complexity leads to a slower rate of expulsion of waste products from cells due to their:
options: Large surface area to volume ratio
questions.explanation: A small surface-to-volume ratio makes diffusion of wastes out of cells slower.

questions.question: Complexity in higher organisms leads to a decrease in their ability to:
questions.explanation: Complex organisms generally have reduced regenerative ability compared with simpler organisms.
